scope: Point-to-point channel coding, capacity and converses, error exponents and finite-blocklength bounds, cost-constrained and Gaussian channels, feedback and memory qualifications; supplemental two-user Gaussian interference-channel constant-gap proof development.

sources.title: Information Theory: From Coding to Learning
sources.edition: Authorized author-hosted Cambridge University Press book draft, identified by the author page as CUP 2023+; the PDF title page says First edition, internal metadata is dated 2024-08-16. It is not treated as the final published edition.
sources.extraction: mutool draw -F txt, consecutive page ranges; all 730 PDF pages extract. Equations are mostly readable, but a subset of math glyphs and line breaks are corrupted in text extraction; PDF page images were checked where the extracted notation affected interpretation.
sources.access_note: The author page states the free draft is for personal viewing/download and prohibits redistribution, resale, and derivatives. The local original is retained only as research evidence and is not committed.

sources.title: Channel Coding Rate in the Finite Blocklength Regime
sources.publication: IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 56(5), 2307–2359, May 2010. DOI 10.1109/TIT.2010.2043769.
sources.edition: Complete author-hosted manuscript dated 2010-10-14; it has 121 PDF pages, which are manuscript pages/figures and are not the journal pagination.
sources.author_page_erratum: Polyanskiy’s author page notes that the analysis of Case 1 in Theorem 48 has a gap and links Cao–Tomamichel’s correction. This source is not used as a standalone valid proof of that step.

sources.title: Comments on “Channel Coding Rate in the Finite Blocklength Regime”: On the Quadratic Decaying Property of the Information Rate Function
sources.edition: Complete author preprint arXiv:2208.12945v2, 2023-04-30; accepted by IEEE Transactions on Information Theory, DOI 10.1109/TIT.2023.3276203.
sources.scope: Complete replacement proof of local quadratic decay of mutual information near finite-DMC capacity-achieving input laws, with a finite linear-constraint extension. The correction is not treated as an unconditional fix for every later theorem using the result; consumers must be rechecked.

sources.title: A Mathematical Theory of Communication
sources.publication: Bell System Technical Journal 27, Part I pp. 379–423 and Part II pp. 623–656, 1948.
sources.edition: Internet Archive scanned reprint with its searchable text-PDF/OCR layer; the 46 physical PDF pages are landscape journal-page spreads, with a blank final page. OCR is imperfect.
sources.extraction: Archive OCR text layer extracted with mutool draw -F txt. The 45 nonblank scanned spreads contain the full article through its Appendix 7; the final PDF page is blank. OCR defects affect some formulas and words. Rendered source spreads were checked for key channel-capacity, noisy-channel coding theorem, and Gaussian-capacity formulas.

sources.title: Two Friendly Proofs of the Berry–Esseen Theorem
sources.publication: arXiv:2602.06234v2 [math.PR], 17 pages, version dated 2026-07-30; arXiv-issued DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2602.06234.
sources.edition: Complete author preprint v2; arXiv identifies the author and version. It contains independent self-contained Fourier-analytic and Stein proofs for independent, not necessarily identically distributed summands.
sources.license: CC BY 4.0 as assigned on the arXiv record; retain attribution to Roman Vershynin and the versioned source.
sources.extraction: Born-digital PDF extracted with mutool draw -F txt. All 17 pages produced text. Equations and the single smoothing-ramp diagram were read; pages 8–9 were visually rendered to verify the third-moment notation and Fourier cutoff, and p. 10 to inspect the ramp illustration.
sources.scope: Complete proof source for the classical univariate Berry–Esseen inequality under independent mean-zero summands, total variance one, and finite total third absolute moment. The Fourier proof is used in r3 notes; the complete Stein proof was also read as an alternative route.

sources.title: Gaussian Interference Channel Capacity to Within One Bit
sources.edition: Complete author preprint arXiv:cs/0702045v2, dated 2007-02-09; 52 PDF pages.
sources.source_ownership_note: The complete PDF and extracted text are existing r5-owned source files referenced read-only; this entry records r3's separate full read and proof supplement. No source copy or hash recertification is claimed.
sources.extraction_note: The r5 source manifest reports 5,973 extracted lines, while the r5 reading ledger and current extracted-text file report 5,921. The full 52-page article is present and was read through the references; preserve this metadata discrepancy rather than rewriting r5 records.
sources.scope: Local proof development of the fixed-split Gaussian Han–Kobayashi inner bounds, weak/mixed one-bit inclusion, Gaussian worst-noise step, and exact strong/very-strong regimes. Weak/mixed results are approximate capacity regions, not exact formulas.

sources.title: On the Han-Kobayashi Region for the Interference Channel
sources.publication: IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 54(7), 3188-3195, July 2008. DOI 10.1109/TIT.2008.924720.
sources.edition: Complete author manuscript deposited on CiteseerX; the local carrier is 14 PDF pages and includes Appendices I-III, references, and figures. The author publications page confirms the final 2008 journal identity; this 14-page manuscript is not represented as the final journal pagination.
sources.extraction: mutool draw -F txt produced text for all 14 PDF pages. Some formulas have OCR/line-break noise; Theorem 2 and Lemma 2 on PDF pp. 4-5 were rendered and checked. No hash recertification is claimed.
sources.scope: Proof source for the seven-facet union description of the Han-Kobayashi region, the fixed-law satellite constraints, the single-cloud distribution switches, and their random-coding decoders. The Gaussian one-bit application and power-shell conversion are developed locally in the r3 proof note.
